I'm using the last measurement on index 2, near the current best, to probe the Sb-doping level in hematite.

content.text:
I submitted index 0 (Fe 0.81, Sb 0.19) as the best composition, with an EQE of 0.055%. That was the highest of the three merit measurements. I don't yet know how it compares with the best composition in the library.

| Index | Fe fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 12 | 0.51 | 0.005 |
| 2 | 0.77 | 0.032 |
| 0 | 0.81 | 0.055 |

- **Index 12 (FeSbO4):** I measured this first because the models looked promising. MACE puts FeSbO4 essentially on the stability hull, and MEGNet predicts a 2.08 eV gap, which is low enough to absorb the 2.7 eV light. Even so, it had the lowest EQE.
- **Index 0 (Fe-rich end):** This was about 10 times better than index 12, which suggests the hematite-rich films are the active ones. MEGNet predicts 2.77 eV for hematite, which would make absorption borderline, but real hematite's gap is about 2.1 eV.
- **Index 2:** I spent the last measurement near index 0 instead of at the Sb-rich end, where there is no hematite. It came in lower than index 0, so EQE rose with Fe content across everything I measured.

Two points on the risk:
- **Index 0 is the library's Fe-richest point.** A composition with a little more Sb (indices 1 or 3–5) could still beat it; the GP suggested index 5 as the next point to try. With only three merit measurements, I couldn't check.
- **The Sb-rich half (indices 13–29) was never measured.** I ruled it out on the downward trend and phase reasoning, not on data.

I used none of the five XRD measurements, so the phase assignments here are inferred from composition, not confirmed.
